audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not match the newer, pre-acquisition cash and debt bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.75 billion purchase consideration at risk in the cash addback ($16.53 per diluted share); $250.55 million annual coupon interest on the $5.0 billion May 2026 notes, before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds June 30 cash raised for CoolIT even though that cash was committed to the July 2 purchase, while forecast OE does not bear the full recurring interest on the acquisition debt.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense generally includes the expense associated with the interest on the Company’s outstanding borrowings, including the impact of the Company’s interest rate swap agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. The $5.135 billion cash balance was temporary acquisition funding, and the filed $4.75 billion purchase consideration equals 19.3% of the $24.617 billion base equity value. The associated notes also carry $250.55 million of annual coupon interest. CoolIT earnings could offset part of the effect, but the current valuation includes neither a post-closing bridge nor aligned earnings.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild cash, debt and senior claims immediately after the July 2 closing; calculate recurring after-tax interest; construct CoolIT owner earnings; and rerun all scenarios on one post-closing perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Ovivo Electronics has only a partial-period earnings and financing footprint in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.596 billion purchase consideration; FY2025 included $3.7 million of sales and a $0.5 million operating loss impact, versus $212.0 million of acquisition-related Global Water sales and a $15.8 million consolidated adjusted fixed-currency operating-income effect in the first six months of 2026; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor contains approximately two weeks of acquired operations and partial financing costs, whereas the bridge and forecasts represent the combined company.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 16, 2025, the Company acquired Ovivo Electronics for total consideration of $1,596 million in cash, net of cash acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its value direction and materiality are unresolved. Adding Ovivo operating cash generation raises OE, while acquisition interest, integration spending, working capital, maintenance capital and incremental amortization-related adjustments reduce it. The supplied record does not provide a full owner-earnings reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-year combined-company OE schedule using Ovivo operating cash flow, maintenance capital, working-capital needs, acquisition interest, integration cash costs and the valuation's amortization policy, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Known future One Ecolab cash charges may be absent from the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: Remaining announced charges computed at $109.8 million pre-tax and $90.4 million after tax; no more than $0.31 per diluted share undiscounted and 0.37% of $24.617 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unmodeled remaining restructuring and special-charge cash payments reduce forecast OE in 2026-2027.
audit_findings.evidence: In February 2026, the Company expanded the One Ecolab initiative and anticipates total restructuring costs of $334 million ($261 million after tax) and special charges of $91 million ($71 million after tax) by the end of 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the pipeline retained or stripped these costs remains unresolved, but the filed scale is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Updated totals are $328 million of restructuring costs and $97 million of special charges, versus $250.2 million and $65.0 million cumulatively recorded through June 2026. The computed $90.4 million remaining after-tax amount is small relative to base equity value and the gap between $85.68 intrinsic value and the $276.92 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace restructuring cash payments through the OE calculation and insert the remaining dated cash charges before crediting further program savings; confirm the rerun changes value by no more than the stated scale.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement obligations may be a senior claim missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $334.4 million net recorded retirement position at June 30, 2026, computed from $533.8 million of pension and postretirement liabilities less $199.4 million of pension assets; $1.16 per diluted share and 1.36% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A residual unfunded benefit claim would reduce the equity bridge, while any difference between accounting pension expense and normalized cash contributions would alter OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The U.S. non-qualified plans are not funded and the recorded benefit obligations for the non-qualified plans were $79 million and $78 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: A bridge omission is possible but not demonstrated because operating cash flow already includes benefit contributions. Even treating the entire latest net recorded position as an additional equity deduction would reduce base value by only $1.16 per share and would not change the conclusion. The specifically cited $79 million unfunded non-qualified obligation is smaller still.

audit_findings.title: TPC litigation is an unquantified contingent claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured settlement, judgment, deductible and defense costs exceeding recorded liabilities would reduce the equity bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the large number of remaining plaintiffs and the fact that many of the claims do not specify an amount of supported damages, any estimate of any further loss or range of losses cannot be made at this time.
audit_findings.explanation: The contingent claim is real, but no supported loss amount or reserve is supplied. The latest filing reports a July 2026 settlement in principle with substantially all remaining plaintiffs and management's view that remaining claims will not be material, which reduces but does not eliminate the uncertainty because settlement terms, insurance recovery and residual claims remain undisclosed. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain executed settlement terms, plaintiff coverage, recorded reserves, policy limits, deductibles, exclusions, insurer reservations, defense-cost treatment and the amount attributable to remaining claims; rerun the bridge for any uninsured amount above recorded liabilities.

audit_findings.title: A discrete 2025 tax benefit may have been treated as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $57.5 million, equal to 4.15% of the $1.3866 billion anchor; computed maximum base-value effect of approximately $807.9 million or $2.81 per diluted share if fully retained as perpetual recurring OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in the FY2025 OE anchor, the one-time tax benefit is grown and capitalized through the operating DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognized a net tax benefit related to discrete tax items of $57.5 million during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion has not been demonstrated because the exact OE calculation is absent. Even under the conservative assumption that the full $57.5 million was retained and capitalized with the base scenario's operating-PV-to-anchor multiple, removing it would reduce base value by about $2.81 per share, or 3.28% of base equity value. That cannot change the conclusion relative to the $276.92 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace all $57.5 million through the FY2025 OE build and rerun after applying one consistent policy to discrete taxes, special gains and special charges.
